Audit and fix the biggest current drivability pain point: binary keyboard/touch steering on the rebuilt Showcase Circuit. User reports that entering corners above very low speed often makes the car continue straight instead of turning. Current evidence: DigitalSteeringInput reaches +/-1 at any road speed, DriverAids.updateSteering ignores forwardSpeedMs, and App.tsx describes a speed-shaped keyboard path that is not actually speed-shaped. Treat AGENTS.md, PHYSICS_CONVENTIONS.md, and M5_VALIDATION.md as hard constraints.

Goal: make keyboard steering physically plausible and controllable without changing mechanical rack authority for mouse/wheel analog input and without hiding a tire/sign bug by adding grip. Prefer a physically grounded digital-input envelope or other input-device emulation, not a speed-dependent mechanical rack stop. Preserve fast countersteer/reversal authority. Add deterministic regression tests covering representative low/medium/high speeds, left/right symmetry, release, and countersteer. If you change physics-adjacent behavior, run test:conventions, test:digital-steering, relevant steering/cornering/transient tests, strict M5 validation, and build. Keep the patch focused.
